# Animated component lists keep membership loads synchronous

## Context
The correction in #19738 introduced a consumer regression while repairing #19717's animated sorting. Grace bisected Institution's `cardIdentity.spec.mjs` with Brain held at `4ec5c03`: Engine `95e058fed9` passes all six cases; `eb2cf2d678` fails the joiner, leave/rejoin and retired-card cases. This blocks neomjs/neo-agent-institution#695 and the Stage59 consumer neomjs/neo-agent-institution#696.

## The Problem
`Animate.construct` wraps the component-list owner's `onStoreLoad`; the new wrapper defers every original load handler to a microtask. A real typed Store + exact-head handler probe confirms that `add` and `clear` emit `load, mutate` with no fine sort, while the owner's rebuild has not run when the mutation returns. Institution's synchronous card-pool/descriptor assertions at lines 136, 173 and 307 are therefore broken. These assertions concern membership, not synchronous browser paint.

## The Architectural Reality
`Store.onCollectionSort` deliberately emits coarse `load` before the collection's fine `sort`; load-only consumers need that notification. `list.plugin.Animate` owns the component-list presentation coordination and must distinguish this coarse sort notification from ordinary membership/replacement loads. The prior repair's motion/record mapping and stale-work fences remain necessary.

Design authority: the existing Store sort/load contract spec and component-list membership consumer tests. Independent triage with Grace retained those consumer assertions.

## The Fix
Identify the coarse notification emitted by `Store.onCollectionSort` and let Animate's fine sort handler own that presentation. Keep ordinary load handling synchronous through the original mount-aware owner, removing the blanket microtask delay and its now-unneeded load serial. Preserve coarse load emission/order and existing sort/filter motion fences.

Prescription checked: `src/data/Store.mjs:onCollectionSort` owns event origin; `src/list/plugin/Animate.mjs:onStoreLoad` owns the consumer's granularity choice. Adding sleeps or changing Institution's assertions would treat the symptom.

## Contract Ledger
| Target surface | Authority | Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Coarse sort-load payload `isSort` | `Store.onCollectionSort` | Marks this load as the coarse half of an actual sort; load-only consumers still receive reordered items before fine sort | Ordinary loads omit the marker and keep their timing | Method JSDoc | Real Store notification-order and membership controls |
| Animate component-list load handling | Existing original owner handler and fine sort owner | Ordinary add/remove/clear/replacement rebuild synchronously; the identified sort load does not pre-reassign components | Existing owner mount handling remains in charge | Method JSDoc | Immediate pool/descriptor controls plus unchanged single-motion suite |

Decision Record impact: none; restores membership timing within the existing Store/list ownership.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC-1: Store still emits one coarse load with current reordered items before fine sort; its sort-origin marker is absent from ordinary membership loads.
- [ ] AC-2: Animated component lists expose correct component membership and descriptors synchronously after add, remove, clear and replacement, retaining unaffected component identity.
- [ ] AC-3: The single-motion component/base-list sorting, record-bound content updates, filter/sort interruption and stale-load controls delivered by #19738 continue to pass.
- [ ] AC-4: Institution's unchanged six-case `cardIdentity.spec.mjs` passes against the repaired Engine candidate; retain the parent/head bisect evidence.

## Out of Scope
Changing Institution's roster expectations, removing coarse Store notifications, adding timer waits, unrelated roster refactors or undoing the original sorting repair.

## Avoided Traps
Waiting one microtask to guess whether a fine event will arrive also delays mutations with no fine event. Suppressing the Store's load globally breaks load-only consumers. A green plugin unit suite alone cannot prove the consumer's card-pool contract.
